label: A label handed back between two people: one person labels another (sees him as a tyrant, calls him a bore, considers him reckless) and then that other person labels the first in return (and he sees me as a slacker); it fires on the returned label's opening ('me', 'as', 'a', 'like'), friendly or hostile labels alike, with or without a sentence introducing the pair. A plain tit-for-tat with no label (I hate him and he hates me), a one-way label, or two people labelling the same third party stays quiet, and it is weak when the narrator is labelled first and answers back.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: A comeback in mutual labelling: in a passage whose earlier sentence introduces two people (My roommate and I clash constantly.), one labels the other (I see her as a slob) and the other labels the first back (and she sees me as a neat freak); it fires on the turned-back target and the word opening its label ('me', 'as', 'a'), with or without 'a'/'as'. Strongest when the narrator labelled first and is labelled back; weak without the lead-in sentence or when the narrator is the one answering back.
